title: RC 桥式移相电路
statement: 图示桥式电路中 V̇_s = 10∠0° V（有效值），ω = 1000 rad/s，两个 R_0 = 1 kΩ，可调电阻 R = 1 kΩ，C = 1 µF。输出电压取 V̇_nm = V̇_n − V̇_m（相量差）。
求 V_n 的有效值，以及 V_nm 的有效值和相位。再分析 R 变化时 V_nm 怎样变化。

questions.ask: R 从 0 调到 ∞ 时，V_nm 怎样变化？
choices: 有效值保持不变，相位从 0° 连续变到 −180°
有效值从 0 增大到 10 V，相位不变
choiceExplain: 这是把 R–C 支路当成纯电阻分压器、又把 V_nm 当成 R 上的电压：那样 R 从 0 调到 ∞ 时它从 0 增到 V_s = 10 V，相位不变。实际上 R、C 上的电压相差 90°，V̇_n 随 R 变化时相位必然改变。
V̇_n = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC) 随 R 变化，而 V̇_m = V̇_s/2 不变，V̇_nm 不可能保持不变：R = 0 时 V̇_nm = V̇_s/2，R → ∞ 时 V̇_nm → −V̇_s/2。
questions.explain: V̇_nm = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC) − V̇_s/2 = (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC)。分子分母的模相等，所以 |V̇_nm| = V_s/2 = 5 V 恒定；相位 = −2 arctan(ωRC)，随 R 增大从 0° 变到 −180°。相量图上 V̇_n 的端点在以 V̇_m 的端点为圆心、半径 5 V 的半圆上移动。

hints: 左边两个 R_0 相等，V_m = V_s/2，与频率无关。
右边 R、C 串联分压：V̇_n = V̇_s·(1/(jωC))/(R + 1/(jωC)) = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC)。
V̇_nm = V̇_n − V̇_m，把结果写成 (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC) 的形式，看分子分母的模。
solution: **1. 结点 m。** 两个相等的 R_0 分压：V̇_m = V̇_s/2 = 5∠0° V。
**4. 一般情形。** V̇_nm = V̇_s[1/(1 + jωRC) − 1/2] = (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC)，|1 − jωRC| = |1 + jωRC|，所以 **|V̇_nm| = V_s/2 = 5 V 与 R 无关**，相位 φ = −2 arctan(ωRC)。
**5. 相量图。** V̇_R 与 V̇_C 互相垂直且和为 V̇_s，所以 V̇_n 的端点落在以 V̇_s 为直径的半圆上；V̇_m 的端点是圆心，V̇_nm 就是半径——长度不变，只转动。调节 R 即可在 0°～−180° 之间移相而幅度不变。

en.title: RC bridge phase shifter
statement: In the bridge circuit V̇_s = 10∠0° V (rms), ω = 1000 rad/s, both R_0 = 1 kΩ, the adjustable resistor R = 1 kΩ and C = 1 µF. The output is the phasor difference V̇_nm = V̇_n − V̇_m.
Find the rms value of V_n, and the rms value and phase of V_nm. Then describe how V_nm changes when R is varied.

questions.ask: How does V_nm change when R is varied from 0 to ∞?
choices: Its rms value stays the same while its phase moves continuously from 0° to −180°
Its rms value rises from 0 to 10 V with the phase unchanged
Neither its rms value nor its phase changes
choiceExplain: This treats the R–C branch as a purely resistive divider and takes V_nm to be the voltage on R: then it would rise from 0 to V_s = 10 V with a fixed phase as R goes from 0 to ∞. In fact the voltages on R and C are 90° apart, so the phase of V̇_n necessarily changes with R.
V̇_n = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC) changes with R while V̇_m = V̇_s/2 does not, so V̇_nm cannot stay fixed: at R = 0, V̇_nm = V̇_s/2; as R → ∞, V̇_nm → −V̇_s/2.
questions.explain: V̇_nm = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC) − V̇_s/2 = (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC). Numerator and denominator have equal magnitude, so |V̇_nm| = V_s/2 = 5 V is constant; the phase is −2 arctan(ωRC), going from 0° to −180° as R increases. In the phasor diagram the tip of V̇_n moves on a semicircle of radius 5 V centred at the tip of V̇_m.

hints: The two equal R_0 on the left give V_m = V_s/2, independent of frequency.
On the right R and C form a divider: V̇_n = V̇_s·(1/(jωC))/(R + 1/(jωC)) = V̇_s/(1 + jωRC).
V̇_nm = V̇_n − V̇_m; write it as (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC) and compare the magnitudes of numerator and denominator.
solution: **1. Node m.** The equal R_0 halve the source: V̇_m = V̇_s/2 = 5∠0° V.
**4. In general.** V̇_nm = V̇_s[1/(1 + jωRC) − 1/2] = (V̇_s/2)·(1 − jωRC)/(1 + jωRC); |1 − jωRC| = |1 + jωRC|, so **|V̇_nm| = V_s/2 = 5 V regardless of R**, with phase φ = −2 arctan(ωRC).

**5. Phasor diagram.** V̇_R and V̇_C are perpendicular and add up to V̇_s, so the tip of V̇_n lies on the semicircle with V̇_s as diameter; the tip of V̇_m is the centre and V̇_nm is a radius — its length is fixed, it only rotates. Adjusting R shifts the phase between 0° and −180° without changing the amplitude.
